findings.disposition_reason: lens-correctness round 2: Per-lens list from reviews/${lens}.json; prints only that lens's ids.
findings.message: The refine loop hands every lens the same prior-finding list built from reviews/*.json (all lenses), then instructs each lens that 'every open prior finding must appear' in its reconciled list. `aegis lens record` rejects an id the recording lens never raised (verified: a correctness report reconciling a security id exits 2 with 'never raised'). Consequence: in any refinement round where at least one lens has a finding, every other lens's re-record is rejected, its record stays on the old digest, check_reviews fails 'did not review this version', and the loop burns rounds without converging — the spec's user scenario (reach a green task gate without hand-editing) cannot complete. The workflow tests only grep for strings, so this path is unexercised.
findings.minimal_fix: Build `prior` inside the per-lens map from `.aegis/runs/${task}/reviews/${lens}.json` only, so each lens is handed only its own ids.

findings.message: Tokens are not checked for shell expansions or git's abbreviated options: `git commit -qm "$(git commit -qam w)" -- .aegis/runs/T-1` and `git commit --inc -qm m -- .aegis/runs/T-1` are exempt. Through the real hook both exited 0 and lib code was committed.
findings.minimal_fix: Exempt only the exact workflow command, matched by a strict regex.

findings.message: The pre-filter needs a bare word `git`, so `\git commit -qam w`, `/usr/bin/git commit -qam w` and `"git" commit -qam w` exit 0 before commit-scope runs. Each committed a product change while the merge gate was red.
findings.minimal_fix: Match git by basename after shell unquoting, not a literal word.

findings.disposition_reason: lens-correctness round 3: Clean tree records files {}; migrate, init and init --force kept it.
findings.message: Clean-tree adoption stores `baseline: {}`, read here and at line 240 as unrecorded, so a later migrate or init baselines post-adoption files. An orphan reading SECRET_KEY then vanished from trace and env.
findings.minimal_fix: Test key presence, not truthiness, here and at line 240.

findings.disposition_reason: lens-correctness round 3: Newlines split segments; the round-2 input is gate and the hook exited 2.
findings.message: A bare newline lexes as whitespace, so `cd /repo`, newline, `git add x.py && git commit -m y` returns index; with only .aegis/runs staged the hook exited 0.

Exemption checks only current dirtiness and bytes: baselined lib/pay.py, fixed and committed by T-1, then reverted to its adoption bytes, vanished from T-2's scope, trace and diff. R-10 exempts only files still uncommitted since adoption.
findings.minimal_fix: Stop exempting a file once any commit since baseline head touches it.

findings.disposition_reason: lens-correctness round 3: bash -c and npm segments now gate; hook exited 2.
findings.message: Segments beside an exempt-form commit are ignored: `git commit -qm m -- .aegis/runs/T-1 && bash -c 'git add x.py && git commit -qm w'` is exempt. The real hook exited 0 and x.py landed ungated.
findings.minimal_fix: Exempt only if every other segment is read-only git or `git add` under .aegis/runs.

findings.disposition_reason: lens-correctness round 2: Refreshed at 844 and 926; round-1 probes stay open.
findings.message: The 'code changed since it was raised' check compares against `raised_digest`, which is set once at first raise and never refreshed. Verified: raise at D1, change to D2, lens reconciles `unresolved` at D2 (or re-raises it by identical content at D2), then a second lens run at the same D2 reconciles `resolved` with no code change → disposition becomes `fixed`. R-1's literal wording is met, but the control it describes (code comment: 'a lens cannot resolve a finding the code did not answer'; ARCHITECTURE.md: 'fixed requires the code to have changed') is defeated: re-running a nondeterministic lens on an unchanged tree can clear a blocking finding, which is exactly the route to a green gate the rule exists to close.
findings.minimal_fix: Refresh `raised_digest` to the current digest whenever a finding is re-raised by content (line 827) or reconciled `unresolved`, so `changed` means 'changed since the finding was last confirmed present'.

findings.disposition_reason: lens-correctness round 2: Transition before focus; refused claim left ACTIVE=T-1.
findings.message: `task_claim` calls `task_focus` before `task_status(building)` can refuse the transition under `parallel_builders`. Verified in a profile-S fixture: with T-1 building, `aegis task claim T-2` exits 2 ('allows 1 task(s) in flight') but leaves `.aegis/runs/ACTIVE` = T-2 while T-2 stays `planned`, so the lease hook now enforces the refused task's lease against the in-flight T-1 builder (its writes under src/orders/** are refused as outside T-2's lease). A refused claim must leave state untouched.
findings.minimal_fix: Move `task_focus(ctx, task_id)` after the `task_status(ctx, task_id, "building")` call so focus only switches once the transition is accepted.

findings.disposition_reason: lens-correctness round 3: Re-raised false-positive kept Alex and reason; reopen sets disposition_by lens.
findings.message: Re-raising by content drops disposition_by/reason, so a human false-positive fails 'without a reason' and a human-closed came-back finding fails 'came back' again. Conversely `unresolved` on a human-fixed finding (921) keeps disposition_by: human, so `next` advised a third patch.
findings.minimal_fix: Carry disposition_by/reason/at when the disposition is kept; set disposition_by to lens on reopen.

findings.disposition_reason: lens-correctness round 3: Runner passes its own reviews/$lens.json ids with the reconcile instruction.
findings.message: The Codex prompt omits prior ids, so its re-review of a lens with open findings lacks `reconciled` and record refuses it.
findings.minimal_fix: Pass the ids from reviews/$lens.json with the reconcile instruction.

findings.message: `--by correctness`, the lens's own name, cleared a came-back correctness finding; only `lens` and `lens-*` are refused.
findings.minimal_fix: Also refuse the record's bare lens name.

findings.disposition_reason: lens-correctness round 2: Rejected at 857; probe exited 2.
findings.message: A round-2 report that omits the `reconciled` key entirely falls through to the absence-after-edit heuristic: verified that after a code change an empty `findings` with no `reconciled` marks an open severity-5 finding `fixed` ('not raised again after the change'). The strict 'incomplete reconciliation is rejected' edge case therefore applies only when the lens chooses to include the list; the workflow always asks for it but the recorder cannot tell a model that omitted it from a first-round runner. The spec is silent here (R-1 is conditional on the list being present), so this is advisory.
findings.minimal_fix: Optionally add a `--reconcile` flag to `aegis lens record` (set by the workflow's re-review step) that rejects a report without `reconciled` when open prior findings exist.

findings.disposition_reason: lens-correctness round 2: Abandoned task printed 'status abandoned'.
findings.message: `task claim` on a task whose status is not `planned` (e.g. `review`, `gated`, `abandoned`) returns and prints 'status building' regardless of the actual status: verified that claiming a task in `review` prints 'claimed T-1: lease enforced, status building' while the manifest still says `review`. The idempotent-on-building case is correct; the message is wrong for every other status and can mislead an orchestrator reading the output.
findings.minimal_fix: Return and print the manifest's actual status after the claim (`checks.load_task(...)['status']`) instead of the literal 'building'.

findings.disposition_reason: lens-correctness round 2: Kinds unioned at 451; packet and plan both tier A.
findings.message: The packet's risk tier comes from declared change kinds only (manifest.change_kinds), while `aegis lens plan` and `check_reviews` use effective kinds (declared ∪ detected). For TASK-UNBLOCK-01 the packet tells the builder 'Risk tier C: mechanical; batched review is acceptable' and records `risk_tier: C` in the packet metric, whereas the plan reports tier A with an independent reviewer required. This is by construction (the packet is generated before a diff exists) and the spec is silent on it; noted only because the two tiers are reported as if they were the same fact.
findings.minimal_fix: No change required by the spec; if desired, label the packet's tier as 'declared' so it is not read as the review tier.
